params.body:
## What changes

A dealer who buys a car from a colleague ("Overkopen") could request its transport only through the button in the purchase mail. The buy-over also shows up for both garages under Bestelbonnen, tab dealer transactions (`order.index.history`, the `vehicle_history` rows), but that row had no transport action.

Now the buyer's row carries the same truck as a customer order:

- no transport yet, or the last one was cancelled: the truck opens the request form (`transport.create/{base64 copy id}`), tooltip "Start transportaanvraag" / "Request transport" / "Demander un transport" / "Transport anfordern" (existing `global.hover_transport`);
- a transport exists: the truck opens it (`transport.show/{uuid}`), coloured by its state, with the state as tooltip (existing `transport.hover_*`), exactly as on customer orders.

The seller's rows get no truck. Neither does a row whose copy is gone (removed from stock, or `new_vehicle_id` empty) or has since moved to another dealer. The R S4-10.1 conditions still apply: without the transport right, the accepted transport conditions and a complete vehicle sheet, the truck stays hidden (`Vehicle::ShowTransport`, same as customer orders).

## How

- There is no second request path. The truck points at the same routes the mail button ends up at (`transport.index?vId=` opens `transport.create` for the same copy) and that customer orders use. `TransportController::create` and `store` only accept a vehicle whose `dealer_id` is the logged-in dealer, and the copy belongs to the buyer, so a seller who opens the link by hand gets 404. That server-side refusal is tested.
- `VehicleHistory::boughtVehicle()` (the buyer's copy, `new_vehicle_id`; the existing `vehicle()` is the seller's original) and `VehicleHistory::transportVehicleFor($dealerId)`: the copy only when the dealer is the buyer on the row and still owns it. `OrderController::history` eager-loads `boughtVehicle.LatestTransport`.
- The truck is one partial, `settings/transport/_row_action.blade.php`, used by both the customer orders and the dealer transactions. It opens the modal through Alpine (`x-on:click="modal.get($el.dataset.url)"`) instead of an inline `onclick`, so `blade_onclick` in `tests/quality-ratchet.json` goes from 249 to 248.

## Business rule

New rule R S4-10.17 (transport chapter, `14-s4-verkopen-aan-een-klant.md`), soort `rechten`. `TransportFromADealerTransactionTest` carries `@rule S4-10.17`.

## Correction to R S5-3.17 and its open point (from #854)

#854 wrote that a bought copy without `trans_path` pointed at derived sizes that were never written, and that 24 photos on 8 copies on production were to be repaired with `stocklist:copy-photo-sizes --apply`. A read-only measurement on production on 29 September 2026, after #854 merged, says otherwise: those 24 photos all had both derived sizes under `_afgeleid/{copy path}/{version}-{md|sm}` (48 of 48 present), and the dry run of `stocklist:copy-photo-sizes` found 0 photos on 0 copies. No copy showed a missing photo. The change in #854 stays correct (a new copy now takes the normal sweep path), but it prevented nothing visible, and the command stays as a safety net.

How those files got there is not established. The code does have writers that make a missing size under exactly that path and version on first request (`VehicleImageService::getImageBinary`, called by the photo app route with a version, the offer PDF in `OfferController::show`, `ShowroomSlide`, and the proposal mail and page through `duurzameUrlVoor`), and `stocklist:fotos-afgeleid --maat` does it for rows of an older generation. Nothing logs which one ran.

Corrected: R S5-3.17 (number and described behaviour kept), a closing paragraph on the open point (status stays `opgelost`), and the two code comments that repeated the claim (`CopyPhotoSizes`, `BoughtVehicleCopy`).

## Checks

- `TransportFromADealerTransactionTest` (7 tests): the buyer sees the truck and requests the transport through its route; the seller sees the row, no truck, and gets 404 on `transport.create` and `transport.store`; a row without a copy renders without a truck; a copy that moved to another dealer is not the buyer's any more; an existing transport is shown with its state and colour, and a cancelled one opens a new request; without accepted conditions there is no truck. Checked that the seller and ownership tests fail when the buyer check is removed.
- Full suite locally: 2359 tests green. Rules*, QualityRatchetTest, PHPStan (no errors), Pint on the new test class.
- Not checked in a browser: the Alpine click that opens the modal on both lists.
params.title: Transport from a dealer transaction: the buyer's row carries the truck
